docs.title: Run the example factory to a merged PR

beats.act: Open the project forge already manages
beats.say: This is the ground the whole story stands on: a real CLI with a real test suite, already onboarded, already merged through once.

beats.act: Press "Architect →"
beats.say: The operator has a feature in mind and no plan for it.

beats.act: Describe the work, cap what this run may spend, and press "Start architect"
beats.say: The ceiling is set before the work starts, not discovered afterwards.

beats.act: Open the session and answer the Architect's questions
beats.say: The interview is where the operator's one sentence becomes something buildable.

beats.act: Read the plan at the gate and approve it
beats.say: This is the first of the two human gates.

beats.act: Go back to the project the plan belongs to
beats.say: The plan is approved.

beats.act: Go to the roadmap, where the approved plan is already being worked
beats.say: The plan is approved, and the factory is already at work on it.

beats.act: Watch the factory plan and build the initiative
beats.say: Approving the plan was the operator's last act for a while.

beats.act: Open the initiative to find the run it produced
beats.say: The card says the work is ready for review.

beats.act: Hand the plan to the build flow
beats.say: The architect has planned and stopped, which is where it is meant to stop — the plan is the first thing a human is asked to approve.

beats.act: Open the flows index to watch the build
beats.say: The build flow is running the initiative now.

beats.act: Open the develop flow monitor
beats.say: This is the surface with per-work-item evidence while a run builds.

beats.act: Wait for the build flow to claim the run
beats.say: Something is genuinely running before anything is held back — the run is claimed and a work item is building.

beats.act: Pull the emergency halt while the run builds
beats.say: One press.

beats.act: The active run finishes under the halt
beats.say: The halt stops new work, not work in progress.

beats.act: Release the halt
beats.say: Release is one press from the same place.

beats.act: Watch the run build
beats.say: The dev station fans out over the work items the plan decomposed into.

beats.act: The built work is assembled for review
beats.say: Between building and judging there is a step that puts the change together with the evidence for it — the diff, the acceptance criteria and what was actually demonstrated.

beats.act: The review station finishes its pass
beats.say: A machine reviewer goes first, against the acceptance criteria and the change class the plan gate confirmed.

beats.act: The review findings are on the run page
beats.say: Its findings are the reviewer's starting point, not its verdict — the human decides.

beats.act: Open the review verdict at its gate
beats.say: The review has an opinion and the operator goes to read it where the decision is made.

beats.act: Anchor one blocking comment to the precedence criterion (the first criterion, said so in the log, when none names precedence) and send it back
beats.say: This is the send-back the whole story is built around.

beats.act: The fix lands on the same branch and comes back for re-review
beats.say: No restart, no second cycle, no lost work.

beats.act: Open the re-reviewed verdict at its gate
beats.say: The fix came back.

beats.act: Read the fix against the criterion, and resolve the blocking comment it answers (the first criterion's, said so in the log, when none names precedence)
beats.say: The operator does not take the reviewer's word that the fix landed — they read it against the exact criterion the send-back named, on the same comment they anchored there, and resolve it.

beats.act: Approve — which is the merge
beats.say: The second human gate, and the only one that spends something irreversible.

beats.act: Reflect on the cycle
beats.say: The cycle ends by writing down what it learned.

beats.act: Open the knowledge graph
beats.say: The cycle is done.

beats.act: Find what the cycle learned on the knowledge graph
beats.say: The theme the reflector wrote is now a node the next planner will read.

beats.act: Open the flows index
beats.say: Before checking what the run cost, the operator opens the flows this factory runs.

beats.act: Check what the run cost
beats.say: One figure, and it is the same figure the event log holds.

beats.act: ACT 2 — open the projects index to start a second initiative
beats.say: A second, smaller change starts the same way the first one did: from the projects the operator already manages.

beats.act: ACT 2 — open gitpulse again
beats.say: The same ground, a second time — nothing here was reset between the two initiatives.

beats.act: ACT 2 — press "Architect →" for the second idea
beats.say: The first change already merged.

beats.act: ACT 2 — describe the second idea and start its architect
beats.say: A smaller ceiling for a smaller idea, set before the work starts.

beats.act: ACT 2 — open the session and answer the second interview
beats.say: A smaller idea, the same interview shape — the architect decides how many rounds it needs.

beats.act: ACT 2 — read the second plan at the gate and approve it
beats.say: Approving the plan is what mints the second initiative — the same act that started the first.

beats.act: ACT 2 — go back to the project for the second initiative
beats.say: Back to the project to start the second initiative, exactly as the first one was started.

beats.act: ACT 2 — return to the roadmap, where the second plan is already being worked
beats.say: The factory claims queued work the same way for every initiative — there is nothing to start again.

beats.act: ACT 2 — watch the factory plan and build the second initiative
beats.say: The second initiative is smaller, but it is planned and built the same unattended way the first one was.

beats.act: ACT 2 — open the second initiative to find the run it produced
beats.say: A second run, with its own cycle id — nothing about it is the first run under a different name.

beats.act: ACT 2 — hand the second plan to the build flow
beats.say: Development starts on the second initiative too — and this time the operator does not wait for it to finish.

beats.act: ACT 2 — open the flows index to watch the second run build
beats.say: Before catching the run mid-flight, the operator opens the flow that is building it.

beats.act: ACT 2 — open the develop flow monitor
beats.say: This is the surface with per-work-item evidence — the run's own detail page has none.

beats.act: ACT 2 — wait for the second run's first work item to start
beats.say: Something is genuinely in flight before anything is interrupted — otherwise stopping mid-flight proves nothing.

beats.act: ACT 2 — open the second run's own detail page
beats.say: Act 2 starts where Act 1 was watched from: the operator opens the run they are about to stop.

beats.act: ACT 2 — stop the second run mid-flight
beats.say: Things stop halfway.

beats.act: ACT 2 — step away while the stop lands
beats.say: The runner needs a moment to reach the boundary it stops at.

beats.act: ACT 2 — after the stop, the running work item finished naturally
beats.say: The work item already in flight when the operator stopped the run is not thrown away mid-turn — it finishes, because nothing in this product aborts a live turn.

beats.act: ACT 2 — and the next work item never started at all
beats.say: That is the fact a resume has to prove it does not skip — not an assumption this story is making about it.

beats.act: ACT 2 — open the second run's own detail page again
beats.say: Back to the run itself to confirm why it stopped, and then to resume it.

beats.act: ACT 2 — confirm the stopped, resumable state
beats.say: The product says plainly why this run stopped — not a crash, an operator decision — and that it is still here to resume.

beats.act: ACT 2 — pull the emergency halt before resuming
beats.say: The operator holds the factory before resuming the stopped run, to see what the halt does to queued work.

beats.act: ACT 2 — resume via the run's own resume control
beats.say: Resume is not a fresh start.

beats.act: ACT 2 — step back to the monitor before reading the queued run
beats.say: The run page reads its run once; a fresh load shows the state resume left behind.

beats.act: ACT 2 — open the resumed run's detail page
beats.say: A fresh read of the run the operator just resumed.

beats.act: ACT 2 — the resumed run waits queued while the halt is on
beats.say: Resume put the run back in the queue and the halt keeps it there: the run says it starts when the halt is released, and nothing it had done is lost.

beats.act: ACT 2 — release the halt so the resumed run can start
beats.say: Releasing the halt lets the factory claim the queued run; the next beats watch it pick up where the stop left it.

beats.act: ACT 2 — step back to the monitor to watch the resumed run
beats.say: The second attempt starts from what the first one finished, not from nothing.

beats.act: ACT 2 — the finished work item survived the stop and the resume
beats.say: The work item that passed is still passed and its commits are still on the branch — that is the whole reason a stopped run is recoverable rather than wasted.

beats.act: ACT 2 — the unfinished work item resumes, not skipped
beats.say: A stopped run does not skip the work it never reached — it comes back and finishes it.
